reason: Conversation 1 never asked the homeowner to move the stacked dryer. It told them to unplug before checking and, at the end, explicitly warned against forcing the unit out of its stack. It moved through sensible front-only checks (container seating, container filter, condenser) and asked whether the pump could be heard. It then escalated to an engineer with an honest explanation of a sump blockage versus a pump or sensor fault. Conversation 2 repeated the same 'run 20 minutes and check the base' question after the customer had answered it, and then told them to tilt a stacked dryer, which is unsafe and contradicted what they had already said. It also kept guessing at a float switch the customer could not find, and the customer had to repeat their constraints several times before it escalated.
